status: first-party engineering disclosure; no independent audit is claimed

sessionRetention.scope: temporary session ciphertext, one-time intake key, and sealed per-session data key only

controls.name: browser encryption
controls.detail: A fresh AES-256-GCM key encrypts session material in the browser; RSA-OAEP wraps the data key with a short-lived public key.

controls.name: input minimization
controls.detail: After envelope decryption, the service parses the input, writes only a normalized sessionToken to the temporary vault, and overwrites the original input buffer. The account email is retained separately as order metadata.

controls.name: single-use intake
controls.detail: The private intake key is short lived and atomically consumed when an encrypted envelope is accepted.

controls.name: ephemeral session storage
controls.detail: Encrypted session material is stored with a maximum 15-minute TTL in a Redis instance without RDB, AOF, or a persistent data volume.

controls.name: storage separation
controls.detail: Session storage, the durable job queue, and PostgreSQL order records are separate. Durable order storage has no session-token, session-plaintext, or session-ciphertext field.

controls.name: logging boundary
controls.detail: Application security events use event names, status codes, and irreversible fingerprints rather than raw login sessions.

controls.name: explicit cleanup
controls.detail: Completion and failure paths delete temporary session material and close the per-order browser process and context.

controls.name: execution isolation
controls.detail: Each execution launches a fresh browser process and browser context. The durable queue carries an order identifier rather than login-session content; no per-order container isolation is claimed.

limitations: This first-party disclosure is not an independent audit or proof of a specific production deletion event.
A privileged infrastructure operator could theoretically inspect live process memory or temporary storage while authorization exists.
The service master key together with a live temporary-vault record could recover that session; the master key is not deleted per order.
The 15-minute rule does not apply to business records or all network metadata.
Deleting the service copy does not revoke an official ChatGPT login session.

accepted: official ChatGPT session-endpoint JSON containing sessionToken and user.email

keyHierarchy.browserEnvelope: Fresh AES-256-GCM data key wrapped by a short-lived RSA-OAEP public key.
keyHierarchy.temporaryVault: Fresh per-session data key; the data key is sealed by the service master key before entering non-persistent Redis.
keyHierarchy.serviceMasterKey: Longer-lived restricted runtime configuration outside the 15-minute rule; not stored in PostgreSQL, the durable queue, or session Redis.
keyHierarchy.explicitRisk: The service master key together with a live temporary-vault record could recover that session.
